directAnswer: To set up a primary key, define the column(s) that will uniquely identify each row in your table using the appropriate SQL command or database management tool.
summary: Setting up a primary key is essential for maintaining data integrity in relational databases.

sections.heading: Understanding Primary Keys
sections.body: A primary key is a unique identifier for a record in a database table. It ensures that no two rows have the same key value.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: Steps to set up a primary key may vary depending on the database system you are using.

sections.heading: Common Issues
sections.body: Ensure that the column(s) designated as primary keys do not contain NULL values and are unique.

steps.title: MySQL
steps.detail: Use the command: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD PRIMARY KEY (column_name); or define it during table creation with CREATE TABLE table_name (column_name INT PRIMARY KEY);

steps.title: PostgreSQL
steps.detail: Use: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD CONSTRAINT constraint_name PRIMARY KEY (column_name); or define it in the CREATE TABLE statement.

steps.title: SQL Server
steps.detail: Use: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD CONSTRAINT constraint_name PRIMARY KEY (column_name); or specify PRIMARY KEY in the CREATE TABLE syntax.

steps.title: Oracle
steps.detail: Use: ALTER TABLE table_name ADD CONSTRAINT constraint_name PRIMARY KEY (column_name); or define it in the CREATE TABLE statement.

faqs.question: Can a primary key be composed of multiple columns?
faqs.answer: Yes, a primary key can consist of multiple columns, known as a composite key, to uniquely identify a record.

faqs.question: What happens if I try to insert a duplicate key?
faqs.answer: Inserting a duplicate key will result in an error, as primary keys must be unique.

faqs.question: Is it possible to change a primary key after it's set?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can drop an existing primary key and create a new one, but ensure that the new key maintains uniqueness.

caveats: Primary keys must always contain unique values and cannot be NULL.
Changing a primary key can affect foreign key relationships.
